transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Ethan Cole (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Connor (BlueWave Platform), Sara Kim (BlueWave ML), Rajesh Menon (BlueWave Security), Ana Torres (BlueWave DevOps)

Summary:
Quick POC weekly to check onboarding progress, validate access gating for the staging environment, and review early benchmark anomalies. Focus on network allowlist, SSO/SAML + KMS integrations, and a targeted latency run for a 512-token chat workload.

Topics:
- Access handoff status (creds, bastion, allowlists)
- Security docs (SOC2, HIPAA questions, KMS/HSM)
- Benchmark summary (unexpected tail latency spikes)
- Observability: Redwood Console telemetry and token breakdown
- Next steps and ownership

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ethan (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick readout: today we want to confirm the access handoff, go over the bench numbers you saw, and make sure we have any blockers for the pilot greenlight.
[00:12] Liam (BlueWave): yeah, thanks Ethan. i'm on; sara and rajesh and ana are here too. we did the initial creds swap yesterday, but we hit a networking snag when we tried to call the hosted API from the staging subnet.
[00:25] Ana (BlueWave DevOps): to add, the egress rules were blocking outbound to redwood-managed endpoints; we put a temporary open rule to get tests working, but we'd prefer VPC peering or private endpoints.
[00:39] Priya (Redwood SE): got it. that's expected if you're using the hosted endpoints. for the POC we recommend either VPC peering to Redwood Private or using the dedicated connector; both support private egress. did you see TLS errors or just connection timeouts?
[00:53] Ana: mostly timeouts. no TLS errors.
[00:56] Priya: okay that's networking then. we can provide an allowlist of IPs and region endpoints; but since you mentioned HIPAA, i think the long-term path is Redwood Private in your VPC — we can hand off the control plane and you keep KMS in your HSM.
[01:11] Rajesh (BlueWave Security): quick Q — does Redwood Private integrate with customer KMS so keys never leave our boundary? we need that for compliance.
[01:20] Marco (Redwood CSM): yes, we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; keys remain under your control and we can show the attestation notes in the security pack. i'll attach the HIPAA appendix in the follow-up.
[01:28] Rajesh: cool. please flag anything about audit logs, retention, and retention windows — that's something our auditors always ask about.
[01:35] Marco: noted, we'll include retention details and sample audit entries.
[01:38]
[01:45] Ethan: moving to the bench anomalies — sara can you summarize what you ran and the numbers you saw?
[01:51] Sara (BlueWave ML): sure. we ran the standard chat profile: mixed-turn conversations, average 350 tokens per request but we also included a 512-token synthetic test. the issue is tail latency — the p95 is fine around 120 ms but p99 spikes to 1.6s intermittently.
[02:10] Priya: okay. a couple of possible reasons: cold KV cache misses, batching behavior during burst windows, or a variant fallback happening. did you pin a model version or were we falling back to a quantized variant?
[02:23] Sara: we pinned model redwood/gpt-xxl-2026-v1 but the config used the default fallback policy; we didn't explicitly disable fallback.
[02:31] Priya: that could explain it. fallbacks to lower-capacity variants can cause token-by-token lat spikes if a session switches mid-conversation. we'll check the routing logs. can you share the request ids around the spike times?
[02:45] Sara: yes i'll pull those and upload them to the shared folder.
[02:49] Ethan: also, was KV cache enabled for the synthetic test? we saw some teams accidentally run synthetic loads without pre-warming the cache, which inflates p99.
[02:58] Sara: i think we ran it cold; we didn't pre-warm.
[03:01] Priya: okay that's likely the primary factor. we'll run a steady-state warm cache test for 512-token profile and report back.
[03:07]
[03:15] Liam: unrelated but related — can we get a quick walkthrough of Redwood Console telemetry? our product folks want to see token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency.
[03:24] Marco: absolutely. priya, do you want to demo the console?
[03:28] Priya: sure. i'll share screen — (pause, audio note: screen share started) — starting at the per-route dashboard, you can see token consumption by route, top prompt IDs, and cost attribution. the latency timeline has p50/95/99, and you can slice by model, region, and route.
[03:46] Priya: note that our sampling rate is adjustable; for pilot we recommend the medium sampling to keep telemetry cost down but still surface regressions.
[03:55] Ana: can we export CSVs or hook into our observability stack?
[03:59] Priya: yes — there's a direct export and we also support a prometheus push gateway + log forwarding to your Splunk or Datadog instance.
[04:07] Rajesh: on telemetry, we need masked prompts in logs for PHI. does Redwood offer token redaction or masking?
[04:15] Marco: we have configurable redaction rules and can apply masking at the ingestion layer. we'll include sample config in the security pack.
[04:22] Rajesh: perfect.
[04:25]
[04:30] Ethan: circling back to access: ana, what remains for the staging environment?
[04:34] Ana: if we can get the allowlist IPs and a test account with an API key that we can rotate, we can run a thorough smoke and the steady-state bench. also need to confirm SAML SSO for the console users.
[04:46] Ethan: we can provide short-lived API keys for the pilot and also set up service account keys inside your VPC. for SSO, we support SAML and OIDC; we can walk through SAML metadata exchange.
[04:57] Ana: ok. i'll send SAML metadata by end of day.
[05:01]
[05:08] Sara: one more question on batching: do you expose batching policy per-route so we can tune latency vs cost? our latency SLO is 200ms p95 for live traffic.
[05:17] Priya: yes, batching is configurable per model route; you can set a latency SLO and the runtime will choose batching window vs immediate serving. there are knobs for max batch size and timeout. also we have a quantization suggestion engine in Redwood Optimize if cost tuning is needed.
[05:33] Sara: cool. for now we'll focus on ensuring p95 < 200ms when warm.
[05:39] Priya: noted.
[05:42]
[05:50] Ethan: small non-blocker: we noticed some transcription mixups in previous notes — the platform team called it KV cash in one doc, which confused ops — just a heads up, the shared notes might have OCR-like errors.
[05:59] Liam: haha yes, saw KV cash. good catch.
[06:02]
[06:08] Marco: actionable recap: priya will run the warm-cache 512-token bench; ana will provide allowlist and SAML metadata; marco will send security pack; sara will upload request ids for p99 spikes.
[06:20] Ethan: any blockers to scheduling the dedicated capacity demo next week?
[06:24] Liam: none on our side, just align with our PM who is out tomorrow. we can target monday or tuesday.
[06:31] Ethan: great — we'll tentatively plan for Monday 2026-06-27 and send a calendar invite after this call.
[06:35]
[06:40] Rajesh: one last SSO/KMS note — we will need a short write-up showing key custody flow for auditors. thanks for the help.
[06:48] Marco: will include the custody diagram in the pack.
[06:51]
[06:56] Ethan: ok if no further items i'll close. thanks everyone.
[06:59] Liam: thanks all.
[07:02] End of meeting.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mislabels and minor recognition errors (proper nouns). timestamps approximate.
